Start with how you use the window

You can tilt the slats to let in daylight, then raise the blind when you want more of the view. At a sliding door, vertical blinds draw to the side so you can walk through. Start with the way you use the opening, then choose the material.

Real wood brings grain and stained finishes. Faux wood is an option for rooms where moisture is a concern. Hold the finishes alongside the colors in your trim, floors and furniture to see what works together.

We carry Hunter Douglas and Alta blinds and can help you compare the choices for your windows.

Parkland® Wood Blinds

Real-wood slats in painted and stained finishes. Choose a wood tone that works with your trim, flooring and furniture.

EverWood® Faux Wood Blinds

A faux wood option designed to resist warping and fading. Consider it for bathrooms, sunrooms and other spaces where moisture or strong sunlight affects the material.

Custom Metal Blinds

Metal slats in a range of colors and sizes. Tilt them to adjust daylight or raise the blind to see out.

Aria™ Soft Blinds

Soft fabric vanes diffuse daylight and give horizontal blinds a fabric finish. An option when you want adjustable light control with a softer look.

For wide windows and sliding doors

Custom Vertical Blinds

Vertical vanes tilt for light control and draw to the side. We plan the opening direction around the way you use the window or sliding door.

Skyline® Panel-Track Blinds

Wide fabric panels run along a track and stack to the side when open. They give large windows and sliding doors a broad, paneled look.

Luminette® Sheer Panels

Sheer panels with adjustable vertical fabric vanes soften daylight across wide windows and doors. Tilt the vanes to change the view and privacy.

Blind fit and installation

The fit matters when you open the window

Handles, locks, trim and window depth all affect the installation. A blind needs room to tilt, lift or slide without getting in the way of the window or door.

Professional measuring helps confirm the fit. If you're considering blinds for several windows together, we can also talk through the layout and the way you'd like to operate them.

One window is welcome

You don't need a whole-house project to call us. If you're replacing a blind in one room, we'll help you choose for that window and explain the next steps.

For a larger project, we can work through the rooms together and compare where the same material makes sense and where you may want something different.

Questions about blinds

Ask John and Max: (818) 884-5464
What's the difference between wood and faux wood blinds?

Real wood gives you natural grain and stained finish choices. Faux wood offers a wood-style appearance with different material properties, including moisture resistance. We'll help you compare them for the actual room.

Can blinds make a bedroom completely dark?

Closed slats reduce incoming light, but light can still pass through gaps and around the edges. If a darker bedroom is your main goal, we'll discuss suitable shade or drapery options as well.

Can you repair a blind I already own?

We can review the product and available components. Send a photo and describe the problem so we can assess whether repair is possible. Parts availability and the condition of the blind matter, including for products from other brands.
